name: Central Park Station Phase I
award: 2025 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Ulysses Development Group plans Central Park Station Phase I, a five-story building with 156 family apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI and a 5,000-square-foot early childhood education center, on RTD park-and-ride land at 3801 N. Ulster Street next to the A Line's Central Park Station in Denver. It won 2025 Round Two federal 4%, state and TOC credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is the first phase of a planned 500-plus-home affordable buildout on an underused RTD park-and-ride lot, made possible by a 99-year RTD ground lease after 2024 state law let RTD discount land; the ground lease still needs a separate RTD Board vote.

status.label: Credits awarded; in Denver site plan review; construction start not confirmed
status.detail: Denver approved the concept plan on 2025-07-24 and Developing MyCity reported in March 2026 that the project was moving into formal Site Development Plan review, with construction targeted for August 2026 and completion in April 2028. No public record of a financial closing, RTD ground lease approval, building permit or groundbreaking was found as of 2026-10-21.

next_step: Watch for an RTD Board action approving the ground lease to Ulysses, Denver's Site Development Plan approval and building permits for 3801 N. Ulster, a Denver City Council HOST loan resolution, and a bond closing.

key_numbers.meaning: 76 one-bedroom, 50 two-bedroom, 27 three-bedroom and 3 four-bedroom units at 30%, 50%, 60% and 70% AMI.
About $31.5M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 accelerated state credit and $200,000 TOC credit.
CHFA is the bond issuer on the award report; the application had planned about $34M of bonds split between Denver ($10M of city volume cap) and CHFA.

key_numbers.value: 99-year RTD ground lease at about $70,000 a year
key_numbers.meaning: The land stays in public ownership; the applicant values the leasehold at about $1.33M.

facts.value: 3801 N. Ulster Street, Denver 80238 (southwest corner of Smith Road and Ulster Street, westernmost parcel of the Central Park Station park-and-ride)
Five stories, Type III wood frame over slab on grade, about 163,000 gross sq ft, three elevators; masonry, fiber cement and metal exterior; roof designed for future solar
1.7-acre Phase I site zoned C-MX-16, now RTD surface parking; the whole RTD parcel is about six acres with 651 transit parking spaces

Early childhood education space of over 5,000 sq ft, delivered as a warm shell for a third-party operator, with over 7,000 sq ft of indoor and outdoor play space; EPIC is advising on the operator search
105 surface spaces, though zoning requires none at this transit site; 18 interior bike parking spaces
About 750 feet from RTD's Central Park Station (A Line every 15 minutes at peak) and served by bus routes 73 and 105. All households get fully subsidized RTD EcoPasses for their first two years
All-electric with a photovoltaic system (CHFA); NGBS Gold targeted (application)
In a Difficult Development Area (30% basis boost) and the Central Park Transit-Oriented Communities transit area; not in a Qualified Census Tract
About $73 million, with about 185,761 sq ft, per city filings as reported by Developing MyCity

The application planned about $34M of bonds as a private placement with U.S. Bank as construction lender, with $10M of volume cap requested from Denver (HOST) and the rest from CHFA as conduit issuer, and said the request might shrink after the federal 50% test dropped to 25%.

background.text: RTD bought the Central Park Station land from Stapleton Development Corporation in 2010 (8 acres, $1,057,047) and 2012 (11.6 acres, $1,585,082) with federal grant funds. Its westernmost six-acre parcel at 3801 N. Ulster had 651 parking spaces used at under 30%.

Ulysses first approached RTD through its unsolicited proposal process in February 2023, proposing about 800 affordable homes. RTD then issued an open Request for Qualifications in November 2023 and conditionally selected Ulysses after a 90-day solicitation.

The RTD Board's 2024-06-25 agenda carried authority to negotiate and sign a 24-month Exclusive Negotiation Agreement with Ulysses; RTD staff wrote that a future Board action is required to lease the property and begin construction. CBS Colorado reported the Board approved the exclusive negotiations, for up to 900 affordable units.
The 2024 legislative session removed the rule that RTD receive fair market value for its land, letting RTD discount land for affordable housing.

By the 2025 application, Ulysses held an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement and an Option Agreement with RTD for Phase I and adjacent phases. At the urging of CHFA and HOST, an earlier plan for four high-rise towers with over 1,000 units in two phases was cut into four smaller phases, ultimately more than 500 affordable homes.
Phase I is to build shared infrastructure for later phases: the full public open space, a circulation spine from Smith Road and Ulster Street, the early learning center and shared courtyards.

Denver approved the concept plan on 2025-07-24. The city expected administrative approvals including Site Development Plan and permits within about 12 months, and the project was to enter Denver's Affordable Housing Review Team track if awarded.

The July 2025 Phase I environmental assessment found no recognized environmental conditions but a controlled one tied to the former Stapleton airport (petroleum hydrocarbons and nitrates in groundwater), with prior state No Further Action determinations.
DHA's role as special limited partner suggests a housing authority property tax exemption structure (inferred; the application does not say so).
The applicant planned to break ground by mid-2026 with a 20-month build, and to use prefabricated parts such as panelized walls from Milender White's Hudson plant.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award descriptions and annual report list 10 units at 50% AMI (17 at 30%, 10 at 50%, 88 at 60%, 41 at 70%), while the application narrative describes only 30%, 60% and 70% AMI units.
CHFA's award report shows $18,300,000 in CHFA-issued bonds, while the application planned about $34 million in bonds, $10 million of it from Denver's volume cap.

CHFA lists 156 units and the application describes about 163,000 gross sq ft and over 5,000 sq ft of early learning space, while Developing MyCity's report on the city filing describes 150 units, about 185,761 sq ft and about 6,000 sq ft of childcare space.
The application targets a groundbreaking by mid-2026 with 20 months of construction, while Developing MyCity reports an August 2026 start and April 2028 completion.
